explanation: Graph the V, y = |x − h|, against the flat line y = d, and the solution is just where the V sits below (or above) that line. With 'less than' the V dips UNDER the line only in the band BETWEEN the two crossings, giving an AND statement (h − d < x < h + d). Flip the toggle to 'greater than' and the solution jumps to the two OUTSIDE pieces — an OR statement. Drag d up and down to watch the green solution band on the axis widen, vanish, or split.
bullets: |x − h| < d means the distance is small → the BETWEEN band: h − d < x < h + d (AND).
|x − h| > d means the distance is large → the OUTSIDE rays: x < h − d OR x > h + d.
The crossing points x = h ± d are the boundaries you read off the graph.
